Therefore Knight does NOT confront dangers. 
6) Rule: Knight either leads others or responds to a crisis. Given: he does not lead others; hence he must respond to a crisis. 
7) Rule: If Knight either confronts dangers or leads others (but not both), then he is fearless. Knight does neither of those things, so the antecedent is false. Nothing forces him to be fearless; he is not established to be fearless. 
8) Final rule: If Knight is fearless, then he can either save lives or earn a heroic reputation, but not both. Since we have no proof he is fearless (and in fact contradictions arise if we assume he is), this conditional gives no new entailment about saving lives.
